summary: Implemented findNextReadyDispatch() helper function in workflow-handoff.ts, inserted directly after partitionWpsAwaitingNextStage(). The helper scans all WPs for a READY, non-dependency-blocked WP and routes to the agent owning its first active pipeline stage via PIPELINE_AGENT_MAP[firstActiveStage(...)]. Returns READY_FOR_SYNTHESIS when all WPs are terminal; returns null when no deterministic dispatch is possible. Self-routing (targetRole === currentRole) is intentionally NOT filtered.

Inserted findNextReadyDispatch() call as the penultimate step (before final WAIT return) in all five affected handoff functions: getQaHandoff, getSecurityAuditorHandoff, getReviewerHandoff, getReleaseEngineerHandoff, and getDocumentationHandoff.

Added 9 new regression tests in a 'Cross-WP dispatch from non-PM agents' describe block covering: Documentation dispatch, all-terminal synthesis, dep-blocked WAIT, QA dispatch, Security Auditor dispatch, Reviewer dispatch, Release Engineer dispatch, custom active_pipeline_stages routing, and self-routing (targetRole === currentRole).

Updated one existing test that was asserting the old (broken) WAIT behavior — the test 'returns WAIT when WP-002 is genuinely waiting for earlier pipeline stages' was updated to expect READY_FOR_DEVELOPER per the new spec v2.1.0 behavior.
All 1912 tests pass (62 test files).

comments.note: The comment on line 403 ('partitionWpsAwaitingNextStage is consumed by getReviewerHandoff and will be consumed by getQaHandoff and getSecurityAuditorHandoff (WP-004/005)') is now stale — WP-003 (not WP-004/005) completed this work. The comment should be updated to remove the future-tense reference.

getReleaseEngineerHandoff was not exported-tested (not present in the test file's import block). This gap meant any test wanting to call it directly would fail with 'getReleaseEngineerHandoff is not defined'. Fixed as part of this WP by adding it to the import in workflow-handoff.test.ts.

In getReleaseEngineerHandoff, the all-terminal early exit is scoped to releaseWps (not all wpDetails): 'if (releaseWps.length > 0 && releaseWps.every(wp => isTerminalStatus(wp.status)))'. This means that if a project has no release-engineering WPs at all, the early exit never fires — unlike QA/Reviewer/Documentation which use wpDetails.every(). This inconsistency could cause getReleaseEngineerHandoff to miss a READY_FOR_SYNTHESIS return in projects with no release stage. The cross-WP dispatch step 2 now serves as a safety net for this case.

The five handoff functions have slightly different inline comment styles for their WAIT fallthrough steps (e.g., 'Step 5 of §5.2 (Condition 5)' vs plain 'Fallthrough'). The new cross-WP dispatch blocks use a consistent comment style, but it would improve readability if the surrounding comments were harmonized across all five functions.

AC4 PASS: Self-routing (targetRole === currentRole) is NOT filtered. Confirmed at code level — no guard exists — and via test #9 (QA calling, WP-002 first stage 'qa' → READY_FOR_QA, not WAIT).

comments.note: Fixed stale comment at line 403 (now line 403 post-edit): changed 'consumed by getReviewerHandoff and will be consumed by getQaHandoff and getSecurityAuditorHandoff (WP-004/005)' to 'consumed by getReviewerHandoff, getQaHandoff, and getSecurityAuditorHandoff' — removing the future-tense WP reference since WP-003 completed this work.

getReleaseEngineerHandoff uses releaseWps.every() for its all-terminal early-exit rather than wpDetails.every() like the other four handoff functions. This means a project with zero release-engineering WPs will not fire the early-exit from getReleaseEngineerHandoff, relying on the cross-WP dispatch Step 2 (all-terminal branch in findNextReadyDispatch) as a safety net. This is functionally safe but architecturally inconsistent. Consider harmonizing in a follow-up.

[documentation-forward] The JSDoc on findNextReadyDispatch() explains the self-routing design rationale well. Consider adding a brief note in the module-level or function-level doc explaining why getReleaseEngineerHandoff's all-terminal early-exit is scoped to releaseWps (not wpDetails) and how findNextReadyDispatch serves as a safety net for zero-release-stage projects. This asymmetry is otherwise invisible to future contributors.

The five dispatch call-site comments have minor style variations: QA/Security Auditor/Reviewer use 'Step N of §X.Y (Condition N)' numbering while Release Engineer uses no step numbering at all. Not a blocker, but harmonizing these would improve readability.
